ground_truth: Cyst formation in a persistent thyroglossal duct

differential: Thyroglossal duct cyst
This congenital cyst can present as a midline neck mass in children and adolescents.
Lymphadenopathy
Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck are common in children, often due to infection.
Thyroid nodule
Although less common in children, thyroid nodules can present as a neck mass.
Dermoid cyst
This benign cyst can occur in the neck region and present as a palpable mass.
Branchial cleft cyst
This congenital cyst can present as a lateral neck mass, but can sometimes appear more anterior.
eliminated: No diagnoses have been definitively ruled out yet.

differential: Thyroglossal duct cyst

Dermoid cyst
This is a possibility given the midline location and fluctuant nature of the mass, although typically these are more superficial.
Lymphadenopathy
Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck can present as a mass, although the midline location is less typical.
Submental abscess
While there is no reported erythema, an abscess could present as a fluctuant mass in the submental region.
Plunging ranula
Although typically lateral, a large ranula could potentially present as a midline neck mass that moves with swallowing.
eliminated: The mass is superior to the hyoid bone, making a thyroid nodule less likely.
